content:
maria_support: Customer reports console shows 1,500 trial credits on their account but API usage shows no credits applied. Customer says their app is on project proj-8823 and provided request example. Needs urgent help — they hit 4xx auth errors when trying to repro after exhausting paid credits.

dan_engineer: Can you paste the exact request headers + project id they're sending? often this is a billing-project vs runtime-project mismatch.

maria_support: They sent this minimal repro:```POST /v1/outputs
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXX
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rwd-large",
  "input": "hello",
  "project_id": "proj-8823"
}
``` They also said the Console shows credits at org level (org-5543) not per project.

tyler_billing: Quick check: our metering shows tokens consumed but billed to billing_project "proj-8823-billing" for that org. Looks like requests came in without the X-Redwood-Billing-Project header, so they fell back to org mapping which points to a different billing bucket.

dan_engineer: That matches. If the runtime project and billing project differ, console credit display can show on org dashboard but API metering attaches to the billing project. Two ways to fix: 1) have app send header `X-Redwood-Billing-Project: proj-8823` (or the billing project id), or 2) update org->project billing mapping (we can do this migration).

maria_support: Customer asked for exact header example and quick mitigation. Also wants to know if we can retroactively apply credits for the tokens already consumed.

tyler_billing: Header example:```X-Redwood-Billing-Project: proj-8823-billing``` If they don't control headers (eg, using third-party SDK), they can set the project in the request body `billing_project` (supported for server-to-server calls). I'll run a query to identify all meter lines for proj-8823 between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-14 and estimate credit shortfall.

dan_engineer: I'll prepare a tiny migration script to remap the past 14 days of metering from proj-8823-billing -> proj-8823 if billing approves. Also adding a runtime check to log when project_id != billing_project so we can catch this earlier.

maria_support: Customer gave permission to proceed with a one-off credit adjustment if we confirm the mismatch. They also provided a request id: rquest_01H8abcZ.

tyler_billing: billing-bot: metering-export for rquest_01H8abcZ -> https://internal-exports/redwood/metering/1887654321.csv : found 3,420 tokens billed under proj-8823-billing. Estimated credit value: $0.68 (using trial rates).

billing-bot: Scheduled a provisional credit of $1.00 to proj-8823 pending finance sign-off. Ticket BU-5421 created.

maria_support: I let the customer know we've provisionally credited $1.00 and are following up with a permanent mapping fix. They've confirmed they can add the header; asked for the snippet for node/js and curl.

dan_engineer: Node snippet:```fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs', {method:'POST', headers:{'Authorization':'Bearer sk-XXX','Content-Type':'application/json','X-Redwood-Billing-Project':'proj-8823-billing'}, body: JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-large', input:'hi'})})``` curl:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX" -H "X-Redwood-Billing-Project: proj-8823-billing" -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs```

maria_support: Customer said thanks and will test. I'll close once they confirm credits applied and API shows reduced spending. Leaving follow-up for migration script and better logging. :thumbsup:
